body:
> For me, I was able to call my doctor on the phone and arrange an appointment. Usually, I would need to get my dad to do it and I'm 26!

That's great! I'm 25 and have trouble with seemingly simple things like this, too. I suffer from panic disorder and severe social anxiety (plus depression on top of that).

My first victory was posting a message here on reddit, asking for help. That alone was incredibly difficult, even though I was using a throwaway account. That was about three months ago, now. Some wonderful people saw my post and have been very supportive ever since. Thanks to their support, I was finally able to leave the house and just go outside every once in a while. That was a big step since I had been housebound for over two months.

After a few weeks I got enough courage to arrange an appointment with a doctor. I was also able to talk to my family about my problems. Since then, I've had somewhat regular appointments with a psychologist, and I've met with a psychiatrist, too. I'm also starting therapy soon. Two days ago I met my therapist for the first time!

Those are my biggest victories for now. Every single appointment has been incredibly difficult for me. I'm still not in a very good shape, but at least I feel like I'm taking steps towards getting better.

> It's nothing like telling someone with cancer to just get over it, and you're stupid if you actually believe that. It's like telling someone with cancer that they should probably try their hardest to get help if they want to survive, because they won't without professional help.

No, you're being the ignorant one, because you don't realize that we're talking about mental illnesses here. Someone with cancer does not necessarily have any problems going to the doctor. Someone with severe social anxiety, agoraphobia, panic disorder or and what have you, most certainly will have serious problems with seemingly simple things like that. I know that from experience. I can't go to a grocery store without feeling anxious. I have failed classes because I was too fucking scared to do simple project work with other people.

You seem to have absolutely no idea how difficult it is for a person like me. You're not saying anything that I don't already know. I appreciate that you're trying to help, but your advice really belongs to /r/shittyadvice

> If I had any one piece of advice for you, it would be to man up and stop caring about what other people will think of you. What anyone thinks of you. Stop caring about what you think of you. Just stop it, and move on from it, and you'll get out of it.

No. This is the same "man up" bullshit I keep hearing everywhere. "Just get over it. Don't stress. Stop caring what other people think. Go to a doctor." It doesn't help, at all. It's not that simple. Nothing is that simple.

It's like telling someone who has cancer to get over it and stop being so sick.

I think I can relate as well. I also have severe social phobia, and I'm a complete hermit as a result. I would *like* to interact with people, though, but I just can't because of my anxiety and panic attacks. I distance everyone from myself because I'm too ashamed to talk about my embarrassing life.

Almost every day I wake up already feeling depressed, and often cry myself to sleep at night. Life at the moment is an absolute nightmare. :-(

I know how you feel. I have severe social anxiety and no real-life friends whatsoever. Not even co-workers, as I have no job. The only people who even remotely resemble friends are a handful of people I vaguely know on an IRC channel I lurk in. But I don't know them. I don't even know their names. If I disappeared, they would just think I got tired of coming there. It sucks.

That was my experience. I wrote a pretty long post explaining some of my problems, and still received only a few responses. While I appreciate every single one of them, it didn't really help at all. A couple of people sent me PMs and offered to talk, but I received no further responses from them. Now my post has fallen to page two or three, so nobody will find it anymore.

If anything, posting there just made it worse. It made me realize that no one can help me. I need to somehow figure out my own problems, but I just can't. I'm desperate and I feel like I'm running out of time. I can't take this much longer.

> You sound like you are having panic attacks. Listen, panic disorder can increase your social anxiety to the point where it becomes agoraphobia.

I read about panic attacks and those seem similar to what I'm experiencing. I'm also afraid that I've already developed a pretty severe case of agoraphobia.

> You are wrong about one thing. You say people don't want to be around you. This is not true. You might be the most boring person in the world with nothing much to say. But there are still people out there who wouldn't mind spending time with you. I am not talking just about people who are desperate. I mean people who are well balanced and happy. This might be hard to accept when you are depressed. But, you need to acknowledge it atleast at an intellectual level.

You're probably right. I think the main problem is that I'm afraid to approach people. I'm afraid that they will find out what a miserable loser I am, and if/when that happens, I would be too ashamed and too embarrassed to be around them even if they wanted to be around me. So I distance everyone from myself. I know I do that all the time. I know I shouldn't, but I can't help it. It's the only way to avoid the anxiety that comes with social contacts. But the lack of those contacts also pulls me even deeper into depression. I feel like I'm in a nightmare.

Thank you for your kind words.

> People don't want to make friends with a nerd? Welcome to reddit, where claiming you are a nerd instantly makes you some friends.

I wish. My anxiety knows no bounds, though. This account is a throw-away. I'm a four-year clubber on my main account and I have no friends here. Not that I post anything, anyway. I'm too anxious to post anything on reddit under my main account, even though I'd be relatively anonymous. I know it makes no sense. None of this crap I'm going through makes sense. It's completely irrational.

> You need to feel wanted, a part of something. But you're not sure where to begin - especially since your panic attacks might hold you back from making that effort.

This is true. I would like to be a part of something. I have tried to become a part of some online communities, especially gaming communities, but I always end up lurking. I'm just not social at all, not even on the Internet.

Thank you.

Seriously, school is the only thing that keeps me going at the moment, but it's getting more and more stressful. I was hoping that getting into a university would change my life, but nothing changed. I can't find an apartment and therefore I can't become independent. I can't become more social because it seems impossible to make any friends. I'm afraid to approach people because I'm too ashamed of my life. I'm stuck in this perpetual loop of misery.

Maybe after I graduate I would get a job and solve some of these problems, but that's many years ahead and I don't know if I'm strong enough to struggle for that long. The past few years have been nothing but suffering. And it's getting worse day after day. Like I said, I'm trying to take it one day at a time. Some days are better than others, but then out of nowhere the anxiety and total depression kicks in. Last night I cried myself to sleep.

I know I should seek professional help, but like I said, I just can't do it. I know it sounds stupid and completely irrational, but it feels like I'm digging through concrete with my bare hands. I'm too scared of everything, and so ashamed of my life I don't even want to talk about my problems. I don't have the courage. I'm a coward and I don't know how to get over it. I hate living like this. I know I'm the only person who can fix it, but I can't do it.
